title: Auth — Refresh
description: Exchange a refresh token for a new access token (and optionally a new refresh token). 0.2 adds no new payload member: it accepts an optional framework `proof` made by a session key bound to the session at auth/authenticate/0.2 or 0.3, presented alongside — never instead of — the refresh token, and it never advances a session's `expiresAt` past its `absoluteExpiresAt`. See Conformance and Security & Privacy.

refreshToken.description: The refresh token previously issued in a TokenBundle. Consumers verify it server-side; producers treat it as opaque.

scope.description: Optional capability tags requested on the new access token. MAY be narrower than the original session's scope; consumers MUST NOT widen scope on refresh.

Response.title: Auth Refresh — response payload
Response.description: Issued by the auth service when the presented refresh token is valid. Carried in a Trust Task document whose type is https://trusttasks.org/spec/auth/refresh/0.2#response.

session.description: Optional session snapshot. Consumers SHOULD include it so the producer can refresh client-side state (acr changes after step-up, scope changes after policy edits, and the session's `absoluteExpiresAt`) without a separate whoami call.

tokens.description: New access token. If the consumer's policy rotates refresh tokens on each use, a new refreshToken is included; otherwise the producer continues using the previously-issued one.
